$AMPY Q3 2026 earnings: Amplify Energy cuts Wyoming field costs, but California expenses rise

Amplify Energy is pumping more oil and cutting costs in Wyoming while fighting rising expenses and price discounts in California. The oil producer grew output at its two remaining fields by 11% from last quarter, and a pause in offshore drilling turned free cash flow positive at $2 million. Chief executive Dan Furbee kept the full-year operating profit outlook unchanged, and by our math the plan points to daily production rising another 7% in the fourth quarter.

• Oil production from retained fields: 𝟕.𝟒 𝐌𝐁𝐨𝐩𝐝 (+7.1% from a year ago (by our math))
• Adjusted EBITDA (operating cash profit): $𝟏𝟎.𝟖𝐌 (+25.7% from last quarter)
• Bairoil field operating costs: $𝟕.𝟖𝐌 (-27.5% from last quarter)
• Full-year Adjusted EBITDA outlook: 𝐔𝐧𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐞𝐝 (middle of the range: $35.0M)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🟢 Bullish

The story got better because structural tax rebates and royalty cuts improved the long-term cash economics of both oilfields. Carbon injection tax credits doubled expected annual savings at Bairoil to over $20 million, while permanent royalty relief at Beta cut the government's share of oil in half to 12.4% and lifted the price cap to $92 per barrel. One caution: a 24% jump in Beta operating costs and $10 million in hedge losses absorbed Bairoil's savings this quarter.

The question now is whether third-quarter cost pressure at Beta was temporary maintenance or permanent inflation that offsets Bairoil's carbon rebates. If Beta workover costs fade, total field expenses will drop toward the $17.5 million fourth-quarter level implied by the full-year plan; if they stick, Amplify will miss its cost target. Fourth-quarter lease operating expenses in the full-year report will settle it.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐂𝐚𝐫𝐛𝐨𝐧 𝐑𝐞𝐛𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐬 𝐂𝐮𝐭 𝐁𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐨𝐢𝐥 𝐅𝐢𝐞𝐥𝐝 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬
Amplify operates Bairoil, an older Wyoming oilfield where it injects carbon dioxide underground to push up crude oil. In June, the oil producer amended its carbon dioxide purchase contract to earn federal tax credits on larger injection volumes, which directly reduce lease operating expenses, the daily costs of running its oilfields.

In the third quarter, the company injected 58 million cubic feet of gas per day, about 80% above its contract minimum. Chief executive Dan Furbee said that "due to increased CO 2 deliveries above the contract minimum, our estimated annualized savings are forecasted to be greater than $20 million compared to the prior year".

That doubles management's previous $10 million annual savings estimate because higher gas volumes trigger bigger rebates per ton. Bairoil's operating costs dropped 27.5% from last quarter to $7.8 million, the lowest since Amplify bought the field in 2014, while field oil production rose 8.5%.

What to watch: fourth-quarter Bairoil operating expenses and daily injection volumes in the full-year report. Sustaining injections near 58 million cubic feet per day would confirm that the $7.8 million quarterly cost run-rate is permanent.

🟢🟢 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐖𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐑𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥𝐭𝐲 𝐑𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐟 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭 𝐁𝐞𝐭𝐚
After selling its onshore gas fields late last year, Amplify relies on Beta, its offshore Southern California oilfield, for growth. Furbee said a new November agreement called Special Case Royalty Relief "further enhances future development economics and supports extension of the field’s economic life".

Beta oil production climbed 12.5% from last quarter and 16.0% from a year ago by our math, reaching 414,000 barrels. Two new wells completed in June and July, C29 and C16, averaged 380 and 360 barrels per day, and the new November relief cuts the royalty rate on all Beta output to 12.4% while lifting the price cap where relief pauses from $80 to $92 per barrel.

This matters because the prior May relief penalized extra production as output grew, whereas the new agreement lets Amplify keep a fixed 87.6% share of oil from future wells. Both new wells are now set to pay back their drilling costs in 10 months, five months faster than management projected in August.

What to watch: fourth-quarter Beta production and the 2027 drilling schedule in the next release. The full-year outlook implies total daily production will reach about 7.9 thousand barrels per day in the fourth quarter by our math.

🟢 𝐋𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐃𝐫𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐒𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝 𝐓𝐮𝐫𝐧𝐬 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐅𝐥𝐨𝐰 𝐏𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞
Amplify spent heavily in the first half of 2026 to drill offshore wells at Beta, which caused cash outflows of $18.1 million in the first quarter and $12.9 million in the second. Following the July completion of the C16 well, management paused offshore drilling to generate cash and buy back stock.

Capital spending dropped from $20.7 million in the second quarter to $8.0 million in the third, flipping free cash flow to a positive $2.0 million. The oil producer used its cash to buy back 1.6 million shares, or 4.0% of its total shares, for $6.9 million through early November.

What to watch: fourth-quarter capital spending and share repurchases. By our math, the full-year capital plan leaves only $2.8 million of spending for the fourth quarter, which should lift free cash flow.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐇𝐞𝐝𝐠𝐞 𝐋𝐨𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐁𝐞𝐭𝐚 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐎𝐟𝐟𝐬𝐞𝐭 𝐒𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬
"Our third-quarter results demonstrate tangible progress in unlocking the value of Amplify’s asset base, with growing production across both assets and significantly lower costs at Bairoil," Furbee said. While Bairoil costs fell, rising offshore expenses and price hedges kept total company costs from dropping.

• Beta lease operating expense: $14.7 million, up 23.9% from last quarter by our math
• Total lease operating expense: $22.7 million, or 44.1% of revenue, up 1.1 percentage points from last quarter
• Realized derivative losses: $9.7 million, or $14.28 per barrel of oil sold

Bairoil's $3.0 million cost reduction was wiped out because Beta's operating expenses rose by $2.8 million as the company worked to restore water injection pressure. In addition, price hedges locked in during earlier periods forced Amplify to pay out $9.7 million, leaving it with $60.91 per barrel when benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil averaged $85.79.

What to watch: Beta quarterly operating expenses in the fourth quarter. By our math, the full-year cost plan implies total fourth-quarter lease operating expenses must fall to $17.5 million, down $5.2 million from the third quarter.

🔴 𝐂𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐚 𝐑𝐞𝐟𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐂𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐬 𝐖𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐃𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐬
Amplify sells its Beta crude oil into the local California market. The company noted that "refining capacity in California has declined, reducing the number of available outlets for locally produced crude oil and placing pressure on realized pricing".

Before hedging, Amplify's realized oil price fell from $85.41 per barrel in the second quarter to $75.19 in the third. By our math, the discount against the WTI benchmark widened from $7.38 per barrel in the second quarter to $10.60 in the third, and management trimmed the top end of its full-year production plan from 7.5 to 7.3 thousand barrels per day.

To find new buyers, the oil producer is evaluating "offshore buoys, new pipeline connections and trucking options", though each option requires time or transport spending. Management said fourth-quarter price discounts have narrowed and improved its full-year differential outlook by $1.00 per barrel.

What to watch: fourth-quarter unhedged oil price realizations against WTI. A narrower gap would confirm that local refinery closures are no longer worsening Amplify's pricing.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟖 𝐎𝐢𝐥 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐇𝐞𝐝𝐠𝐞𝐬
To protect future cash flow against oil price swings, Amplify added derivative contracts covering 2027 and 2028 output. It locked in 2027 costless collars — contracts that set a price floor and ceiling — with floors of $75.00 per barrel for WTI and $78.59 for Brent, and ceilings of $87.50 and $93.99. It also hedged 20% to 25% of expected 2028 production from existing wells using Brent swaps at $75.50.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐁𝐈𝐓𝐃𝐀 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏𝟎.𝟖 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Operating profit before interest, taxes, depreciation and one-offs rose 25.7% from $8.6 million in the second quarter and nearly tripled from $3.8 million in the first quarter. As a share of revenue, it expanded to 21.1% from 16.4% last quarter, driven by higher oil volumes and Bairoil cost rebates.

𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐞𝐪𝐮𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏𝟎.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Cash on hand fell 53.1% from $21.2 million at the end of June and $41.5 million in March, as the company funded working capital shifts, $8.0 million of capital projects, and share buybacks. Amplify still carries zero debt on its credit facility and holds $25.0 million in total liquidity.

𝐀𝐜𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟐𝟐.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Money owed by customers for oil sales grew 12.4% from $19.5 million last quarter, even though total revenue before hedges dipped 2.4% to $51.4 million. Across the broader balance sheet, working capital changes tied up $7.3 million of cash in the third quarter, limiting operating cash flow to $3.1 million.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐍𝐞𝐭 𝐀𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞 𝐃𝐚𝐢𝐥𝐲 𝐎𝐢𝐥 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝟕.𝟎–𝟕.𝟑 𝐌𝐁𝐛𝐥𝐬/𝐝  ⇗ accelerating
🠇 cut from 7.0–7.5 MBbls/d
Cut at the top end. The middle of the full-year range moved down by 100 barrels per day to 7.15 thousand barrels per day. By our math, that still implies fourth-quarter output of about 7.9 thousand barrels per day, up 7.3% from the third quarter. It is the second consecutive trim to the midpoint: -50 barrels per day in August, and -100 in November.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐎𝐢𝐥 𝐃𝐢𝐟𝐟𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐚𝐥 (𝐔𝐧𝐡𝐞𝐝𝐠𝐞𝐝): $(𝟖.𝟎𝟎)–$(𝟏𝟎.𝟎𝟎) / 𝐁𝐛𝐥  ⇗ accelerating
🠅 raised from $(9.00)–$(11.00) / Bbl
Raised. Management narrowed its expected full-year price discount against WTI by $1.00 per barrel, putting the middle of the range at a $9.00 discount. In August, the oil producer had widened this discount from a prior range of $6.00 to $9.00 because of California refinery closures, but fourth-quarter pricing has improved.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐋𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐞: $𝟖𝟎.𝟎–$𝟗𝟎.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from $80.0–$95.0 million
Improved. Amplify lowered the top end of its full-year field cost outlook by $5.0 million, bringing the middle of the range down to $85.0 million. By our math, after $67.5 million of expenses in the first nine months, the midpoint implies fourth-quarter costs of $17.5 million, down 22.9% from the third quarter. This is the second $2.5 million midpoint reduction in a row.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐓𝐚𝐱𝐞𝐬 (% 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞): 𝟔.𝟎%–𝟕.𝟎%  ⇒ stable
🠇 cut from 5.0%–7.0%
Tightened upward. The bottom of the range for production, property and franchise taxes rose by 1.0 percentage point, moving the midpoint to 6.5% of revenue. Third-quarter taxes were 6.2% of revenue, up from 5.8% in the second quarter.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐆𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠, 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐜𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬: $𝟑.𝟎–$𝟑.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇒ stable
🠇 cut from $2.0–$3.0 million
Tightened to the high end. The company fixed its full-year transport cost outlook at $3.0 million, up $0.5 million at the middle of the range. Through the first nine months of 2026, transport expenses totaled $2.5 million by our math.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐆𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐥 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐀𝐝𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞: $𝟐𝟎.𝟎–$𝟐𝟐.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠇 cut from $17.0–$22.0 million
Tightened upward. Management lifted the bottom of the overhead cost range by $3.0 million, raising the midpoint to $21.0 million. After spending $16.0 million in the first three quarters, the middle of the range leaves $5.0 million for the fourth quarter by our math, compared with $4.6 million in the third.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐁𝐈𝐓𝐃𝐀: $𝟑𝟎.𝟎–$𝟒𝟎.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
🠆 unchanged from $30.0–$40.0 million
Unchanged. The full-year operating cash profit plan stays at a midpoint of $35.0 million, assuming $90 WTI oil for the rest of the year. By our math, subtracting the $23.2 million earned in the first nine months leaves $11.8 million for the fourth quarter, up 8.9% from the third quarter.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐞: $𝟑.𝟎–$𝟒.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇒ stable
🠆 unchanged from $3.0–$4.0 million
Unchanged. Full-year cash interest costs, which mainly consist of surety bond premiums for the offshore Beta field, remain at a $3.5 million midpoint. Nine-month cash interest totaled $2.6 million, leaving about $0.9 million for the fourth quarter by our math.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐈𝐧𝐯𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭: $𝟓𝟎.𝟎–$𝟓𝟓.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠇 cut from $45.0–$55.0 million
Tightened upward. The bottom of the capital spending range rose by $5.0 million, moving the middle of the range up $2.5 million to $52.5 million. Because Amplify has already invested $49.7 million year to date, the midpoint leaves just $2.8 million of spending for the fourth quarter by our math, down from $8.0 million in the third.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐁𝐞𝐭𝐚 𝐒𝐢𝐧𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐅𝐮𝐧𝐝: $𝟗.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇒ stable
🠆 unchanged from $9.0 million
Unchanged. Amplify will contribute $9.0 million this year into the dedicated decommissioning fund for its offshore Beta platforms, unchanged since the start of the year.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐮𝐫𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐬𝐞: $𝟔.𝟎–$𝟏𝟓.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
🠅 raised from $0.0–$15.0 million
Raised at the bottom end. The floor of the buyback range moved up to $6.0 million to reflect the $6.9 million of stock already repurchased through early November, leaving up to $8.1 million under the current authorization through December 31.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐝𝐢𝐝 𝐁𝐞𝐭𝐚 𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐜𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐣𝐮𝐦𝐩 𝟐𝟒% 𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫?
Beta lease operating expenses rose from $11.9 million in the second quarter to $14.7 million in the third. Management mentioned waterflood pressure maintenance and workovers, but did not state how much of that $2.8 million increase is one-time versus permanent.

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐡𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐲𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝟓𝟓 𝐰𝐞𝐥𝐥 𝐚𝐭 𝐁𝐞𝐭𝐚?
In the first quarter, Amplify said the C55 well hit an over-pressured zone and would be completed in the second or third quarter. The third-quarter release detailed results for C29 and C16, but did not mention C55.

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐯𝐨𝐥𝐮𝐦𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐝𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐧𝐞𝐰 𝐫𝐨𝐲𝐚𝐥𝐭𝐲 𝐫𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐟?
Amplify secured a 12.4% royalty rate on all Beta production starting November 1, subject to certain volume and price thresholds detailed in the 10-Q filing. The release gave the $92 per barrel price cap, but omitted the minimum production volume required.

𝐖𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐛𝐚𝐧𝐤𝐬 𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 $𝟐𝟓 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐛𝐨𝐫𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐛𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫?
Amplify is completing its semi-annual credit facility redetermination later in the fourth quarter. With cash down to $10.0 million and the company planning to continue share buybacks, any change to the $15.0 million elected commitment affects available liquidity.

$GNRC KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM GENERAC’S Q3 2026 EARNINGS CALL

Generac’s call provides strong evidence that data center investment is translating into equipment commitments, rather than remaining confined to announced development plans. Approximately $4.5 billion of backlog, almost $600 million of recent non-hyperscale orders, and expected 2027 data center revenue well above $2 billion support positive read-throughs for engine suppliers, alternator manufacturers, and complementary electrical infrastructure providers. The more differentiated implications concern who captures the economics: constrained component suppliers, creditworthy customers able to secure production slots, and equipment vendors whose products remain necessary regardless of which generator manufacturer wins. Negative implications center on incumbent generator suppliers’ competitive protection, financing requirements for capital-intensive developers, regulatory exposure within foreign-controlled supply chains, and continued residential solar weakness. Generac’s projected growth should not be extrapolated directly to industry growth because market-share gains and new capacity are significant contributors. Impact assessments below refer to business fundamentals and earnings sensitivity, not predicted share-price movements.

POWER GENERATION AND COMPONENTS

ENGINE SUPPLY IS THE MOST DIRECT UPSTREAM BENEFICIARY OF GENERAC’S EXPANSION (READ-THROUGH 1)

Affected company: Weichai Power (https://t.co/SLZ3yvHdIp: China). Directional impact: positive. Magnitude: high for the Baudouin high-horsepower engine franchise and potentially meaningful, but not quantifiable from this call, for consolidated earnings.

The strongest supporting disclosure was management’s statement that major components are being dual- or triple-sourced “with the exception of the engine at this point.” This accompanies a planned increase in annual data center production capacity from approximately $1.25 billion exiting 2026 to approximately $4 billion during 2027. Expected data center revenue increases from nearly $500 million in 2026 to well above $2 billion in 2027.

The supplier relationship is established independently of inference from the call. Weichai America identifies Baudouin as Generac’s North American engine partner for M33 and M55 engines packaged at Oshkosh. Generac’s published large-generator specifications identify Baudouin M55 engines. Consequently, the transmission mechanism is direct: increased production of those generator platforms requires increased engine procurement, raising Baudouin’s shipment volumes, factory utilization, and potential fixed-cost absorption.

The important distinction is between engine demand and generator assembly capacity. Generac can add assembly shifts relatively cheaply, but that capacity cannot produce saleable systems without qualified engines. Current engine-source dependence gives Baudouin a stronger position than an interchangeable enclosure or ancillary component supplier. It does not establish contractual exclusivity, guaranteed pricing increases, or an entitlement to the full value of Generac’s backlog. Engine revenue represents only part of the completed system’s value.

The near-term catalyst is evidence of engine deliveries supporting Sussex’s Q4 ramp and the larger 2027 production schedule. The longer-duration implication is a more substantial data center earnings stream within an engine supplier otherwise associated with broader industrial and transportation cycles. The operating read-through is strongly positive, but the regulatory exposure discussed below prevents treating this as an uncomplicated beneficiary.

ALTERNATORS PROVIDE A LESS OBVIOUS DIRECT EXPOSURE, AND THE OWNERSHIP ATTRIBUTION MATTERS (READ-THROUGH 2)

Affected company: WEG (WEGE3: Brazil). Directional impact: positive. Magnitude: high for the relevant large-generator product line and moderate for the diversified group.

Generac’s expected increase to well above $2 billion of 2027 data center revenue, alongside its planned capacity expansion, supports demand for large alternators as well as engines. Generac’s published data center product materials identify Marathon DataMAX alternators on its large diesel generator platform. Marathon’s industrial motors and generators business transferred from Regal Rexnord (RRX: United States) to WEG in 2024. The direct Marathon exposure therefore belongs to WEG, not Regal Rexnord.

The transmission mechanism is increased component demand per completed generator system. Higher shipments support manufacturing utilization and absorption of engineering and production overhead. The opportunity is not dependent on increased generator operating hours after installation: the alternator is required when the system is built, even if emergency runtime subsequently remains limited.

The competitive position differs from Baudouin’s. Management explicitly described efforts to dual- and triple-source major components other than engines. WEG should therefore benefit from the disclosed platform relationship, but its future share of Generac’s procurement cannot be assumed constant. The call supports a volume opportunity more strongly than it supports exceptional pricing power.

The near-term trading catalyst is confirmation that large-generator orders and shipments are tracking Generac’s production expansion. The fundamental benefit extends through 2027-2028 as qualified component capacity is deployed. The geographic implication is important: a US AI infrastructure spending cycle can generate earnings for a Brazilian-listed industrial supplier through an established North American manufacturing franchise. This is a more specific exposure than a general emerging-market industrial growth thesis.

INCUMBENT GENERATOR SUPPLIERS FACE LESS EXCLUSIVITY, NOT NECESSARILY LOWER INDUSTRY DEMAND (READ-THROUGH 3)

Affected companies: Caterpillar (CAT: United States), Cummins (CMI: United States), and Rolls-Royce Holdings (RR.: United Kingdom). Directional impact: negative for relative competitive positioning and long-duration scarcity assumptions. Magnitude: limited immediate earnings impact, but potentially moderate strategic and valuation significance.

Generac disclosed approximately $4.5 billion of data center backlog, expected Amazon deliveries of $2.4 billion during 2027-2028, and discussions with an additional hyperscaler. Management also described approximately $4 billion of planned annual capacity and preliminary consideration of what $6 billion would require.

The relevant negative read-through is not that the incumbent suppliers’ existing orders disappear. It is that another qualified supplier is moving from marginal participation to commercially significant scale. Hyperscaler qualification, demonstrated supply-chain capability, and a larger service footprint reduce customers’ dependence on a narrow supplier group. Over time, additional qualified supply improves customers’ ability to negotiate delivery schedules, diversify procurement, and resist unfavorable commercial terms.

This distinction matters most when evaluating the durability of unusually favorable pricing and backlog economics. A larger Generac can win incremental programs even while Caterpillar, Cummins, and Rolls-Royce continue growing in absolute terms. The competitive headwind is therefore more credible than a near-term industry downturn thesis.

Near-term earnings are protected by strong demand and existing backlog. The more important catalysts are successful delivery under the Amazon program, qualification with another hyperscaler, and subsequent procurement awards for 2028 and beyond. Those developments would demonstrate that Generac’s competitive position is durable rather than a temporary response to incumbent lead times. The call supports greater caution toward indefinite scarcity premiums, not an automatic short recommendation on the incumbent manufacturers.

FOREIGN-CONTROLLED ENGINE SOURCING CREATES A DISTINCT REGULATORY EVENT RISK (READ-THROUGH 4)

Affected company: Weichai Power (https://t.co/SLZ3yvHdIp: China). Potential relative beneficiaries under an adverse sourcing outcome: Caterpillar (CAT: United States), Cummins (CMI: United States), and Rolls-Royce Holdings (RR.: United Kingdom), subject to their own component sourcing and qualification requirements. Directional impact: negative risk exposure for Weichai; conditional competitive benefit for alternatives. Magnitude: potentially high for the affected US data center engine business, but the regulatory outcome remains unresolved.

Management argued that the executive order targeting foreign-sourced bulk-power equipment should not capture its backup generators. Jagdfeld stated, “Our generators are not connected to the grid. They’re connected to the facility.” Nevertheless, management also acknowledged uncertainty over final implementation and discussed accelerating potential domestic engine production if the interpretation becomes unfavorable.

The important legal distinction is that the 69,000-volt reference is not a universal exemption for every lower-voltage component. The August 26 executive order’s equipment definition includes backup generators when used within the covered bulk-power system. Its application depends on the equipment’s function, the relevant foreign-entity nexus, and implementing rules. A French engine brand, European production, or UK-manufactured controls does not by itself resolve every ownership and supply-chain question.

The transmission mechanism could involve procurement restrictions, additional compliance requirements, sourcing changes, or delayed customer approvals. These can affect orders and delivery timing without requiring an outright ban. Establishing US engine production could mitigate certain risks, but would require investment, staffing, qualification, and regulatory acceptance. It is not an immediately available substitute for current supply.

December implementation guidance is the identifiable near-term catalyst. The longer-duration issue is whether customer procurement standards become more restrictive even where equipment remains legally permissible. The high-conviction conclusion is that this risk is concentrated and commercially relevant, not that an adverse ruling is inevitable. The same Generac backlog that strengthens Weichai’s operating outlook increases the significance of the policy question.

ELECTRICAL INFRASTRUCTURE

COMPLEMENTARY POWER EQUIPMENT BENEFITS WITHOUT NEEDING TO PICK THE WINNING GENERATOR MANUFACTURER (READ-THROUGH 5)

Affected companies: Eaton (ETN: Ireland), Schneider Electric (SU: France), and Vertiv (VRT: United States). Directional impact: positive. Magnitude: moderate consolidated fundamental support, with greater significance in their data center electrical businesses.

The call reported almost $600 million of recent non-hyperscale orders, repeat orders for additional project phases, and orders across multiple continents. Generac is expanding production in Europe, Asia, and Latin America specifically to support secured demand. These disclosures provide evidence of a broader project pipeline than the Amazon agreement alone.

The transmission mechanism is complementary equipment demand. A functioning data center requires power distribution, protection, transfer equipment, UPS systems, and associated controls alongside backup generation. Increasing the number of qualified generator suppliers does not eliminate these requirements. Eaton and Schneider participate across substantial portions of the electrical distribution chain, while Vertiv participates in critical power, UPS, and integrated infrastructure.

The non-consensus distinction is that competitive pressure among generator manufacturers can coexist with attractive demand for the rest of the power system. Even if Generac captures share from another genset supplier, the associated project still needs complementary electrical equipment. These companies can therefore participate in the underlying buildout without depending on a particular generator OEM retaining share.

The geographic evidence also matters. Orders supporting European, Asian, and Latin American expansion reinforce the relevance of global manufacturing and service networks, rather than an exclusively US domestic capacity thesis.

The near-term implication is supportive evidence for project execution and order durability over the next several reporting periods. The longer-duration benefit is conversion of that pipeline into equipment shipments and service opportunities during 2027-2028. Generac’s projected revenue growth should not be applied directly to these companies, and none was identified as the supplier to the specific Amazon programs. The read-through supports sector demand, not undisclosed contract awards or automatic estimate increases.

HYPERSCALERS AND DATA CENTER OPERATORS

AMAZON GAINS PROCUREMENT FLEXIBILITY AND SUPPLIER ALIGNMENT, RATHER THAN A NEW SOURCE OF GRID POWER (READ-THROUGH 6)

Affected company: https://t.co/SpqvHNV5fi (AMZN: United States). Directional impact: positive. Magnitude: moderate strategic significance for infrastructure delivery, but low direct consolidated earnings significance.

Generac expects $2.4 billion of deliveries to Amazon during 2027-2028. The agreement also provides warrants covering approximately 1.7 million shares, with future vesting linked to cumulative qualifying purchases reaching $8 billion. Management said Amazon had conducted extensive supply-chain diligence.

The principal benefit is improved access to qualified backup equipment. An additional large-scale supplier reduces dependence on a small incumbent group and can improve procurement flexibility. The warrant creates an economic link between customer purchases and supplier value, while giving Generac a strong incentive to execute and expand capacity.

The value should not be confused with free equipment or a firm $8 billion order. The $8 billion amount is associated with warrant vesting, and the equity instrument has exercise conditions and an exercise price. Nor do backup generators solve the need for continuous electricity supply, utility interconnection, or timely completion of the rest of a data center.

The agreement was announced before this earnings call. The incremental information is therefore Generac’s production progress and greater visibility into delivery capacity, not the existence of a newly disclosed Amazon commitment. Near-term trading relevance is limited unless those execution updates materially alter deployment expectations.

The longer-duration benefit is reduced procurement concentration and greater scheduling resilience. Successful delivery could help prevent backup equipment from becoming a commissioning bottleneck. It does not independently justify an increase in Amazon revenue forecasts or an assumption that the generator purchase amount represents incremental spending above previously planned infrastructure budgets.

SUPPLIER CREDIT STANDARDS FAVOR WELL-FUNDED DEVELOPERS OVER FINANCING-DEPENDENT CAPACITY PLANS (READ-THROUGH 7)

Affected companies: Digital Realty Trust (DLR: United States) and Equinix (EQIX: United States), relatively positive; Applied Digital (APLD: United States) and CoreWeave (CRWV: United States), relatively negative for funding flexibility and delivery risk. Magnitude: moderate for development economics and capital requirements, with potentially greater consequences where equipment availability determines project completion.

Management’s most consequential credit comment was that a customer unwilling to provide an acceptable corporate guarantee for an SPV would not receive business: “we’re not going to do it.” Management also emphasized customer deposits and payment schedules that protect Generac’s exposure. Separately, it reported almost $600 million of recent non-hyperscale orders and increasing discussions with larger REIT-backed customers.

The combined signal is not a broad collapse in colocation demand. It is a market in which equipment suppliers can increasingly discriminate among customers based on credit quality and willingness to fund procurement commitments. Digital Realty and Equinix have established operating platforms and broad capital-market access. Those attributes can improve their ability to secure equipment and execute projects relative to less mature or more financing-dependent developers.

The negative transmission for Applied Digital is through development funding requirements. More upfront deposits or sponsor support can increase capital committed before rental income begins, constrain the amount of development supported by a given equity contribution, and reduce flexibility to rely entirely on project-level financing. Strong tenant commitments and financing partners can mitigate those effects, but do not make procurement funding irrelevant.

For CoreWeave, the transmission can be indirect because landlords and development partners procure substantial portions of the physical infrastructure. Tighter supplier requirements can still emerge as higher development costs, higher lease charges, additional commitments, or delays in capacity becoming available. The call does not establish that either company is a Generac customer or has been refused supply.

Near-term catalysts are financing announcements, project funding terms, and revisions to delivery schedules. The longer-duration implication is a greater competitive advantage for access to capital and demonstrable execution. Growing demand and tightening credit standards can coexist: strong orders do not prove that every announced project is equally financeable.

EMISSIONS REQUIREMENTS RAISE THE COST OF DEVELOPABLE CAPACITY EVEN WHEN BACKUP GENERATORS RARELY RUN (READ-THROUGH 8)

Affected companies: Digital Realty Trust (DLR: United States) and Equinix (EQIX: United States), with similar exposure for https://t.co/SpqvHNV5fi (AMZN: United States) on self-developed sites. Directional impact: negative for affected project costs and execution timelines. Magnitude: generally low to moderate at the portfolio level, but potentially high for an individual project whose approval or completion is delayed.

Management said a meaningful portion of backlog already includes requirements more stringent than the federal baseline for emergency diesel generation. Customers and local jurisdictions are requesting additional emissions-control technology, including equipment intended to achieve Tier 4-type performance. Generac also acknowledged supply constraints and the need to expand its aftertreatment supply base.

The transmission mechanism is additional installed cost and execution complexity. Catalysts, particulate filtration, associated controls, and packaging requirements increase the equipment bill and introduce further procurement and commissioning tasks. These costs are incurred even where actual emergency operating hours are low. For a developer, higher construction cost reduces the stabilized development yield unless rents or customer contributions compensate.

The higher-consequence risk is timing. Technical ability to supply an emissions-compliant generator does not ensure timely approval of the entire site. Where a project’s critical path includes air permitting or delivery of specialized aftertreatment equipment, delays can defer rental commencement or usable compute capacity while financing and construction costs continue.

The geographic signal is strongest in jurisdictions with stricter air-quality requirements, including California and selected East Coast markets identified in the call. Management characterized the trend as continuing irrespective of election outcomes. Underwriting a near-term regulatory reversal would therefore be inconsistent with the operating evidence.

Near-term catalysts are site-specific permits, equipment specifications, and delivery schedules rather than broad federal political headlines. The longer-duration implication is a higher value for already-permitted locations, proven project designs, and repeatable compliance processes. This qualifies the positive data center demand outlook without implying that diesel backup is being broadly displaced.

CONSTRUCTION AND EQUIPMENT RENTAL

MOBILE EQUIPMENT DEMAND SUPPORTS RENTAL COMPANIES’ LARGE-PROJECT PIPELINES (READ-THROUGH 9)

Affected companies: United Rentals (URI: United States) and Herc Holdings (HRI: United States). Directional impact: positive. Magnitude: moderate for large-project and specialty-rental demand, but smaller for consolidated earnings than Generac’s data center growth rates might suggest.

Generac reported another quarter of growth in mobile equipment sales to national and independent rental customers. The acquired Allmand business exceeded expectations for both revenue and profitability. Management attributed demand partly to a substantial pipeline of large construction projects and anticipated continued strong mobile product growth in 2027.

The transmission mechanism is deployment of rental equipment into project activity. Data center and other large industrial construction sites require temporary power, lighting, environmental control, and related services before permanent infrastructure is commissioned. Sustained project starts can support rental utilization, duration, and ancillary service revenue for national operators with broad fleets and service coverage.

This is a different timing exposure from the permanent generator opportunity. Rental activity can monetize construction well before a completed data center produces revenue for its owner. It also does not depend on whether the permanent installation ultimately uses Generac, Caterpillar, Cummins, or another supplier.

The evidence should not be overstated. Generac explicitly attributed part of Allmand’s performance to increased market share following integration. Supplier shipment growth therefore does not translate directly into the same rate of industry fleet spending. Moreover, increased equipment purchases initially consume rental-company cash; returns depend on utilization, pricing, maintenance costs, and eventual residual values.

The near-term read-through supports activity and fleet deployment through the end of 2026 and into 2027. The longer-duration benefit depends on continued construction sequencing, not on the operating hours of completed backup generators. The call is more supportive of large-project and specialty demand than of a broad recovery in all local construction markets.

RESIDENTIAL SOLAR AND STORAGE

STRONGER RESILIENCE DEMAND IS NOT TRANSLATING INTO A GENERAL RESIDENTIAL SOLAR RECOVERY (READ-THROUGH 10)

Affected companies: Enphase Energy (ENPH: United States) and SolarEdge Technologies (SEDG: Israel). Directional impact: negative for near-term residential equipment demand expectations. Magnitude: moderate for Enphase’s exposed residential business and more geographically qualified for SolarEdge.

Generac reported mid-teens home standby shipment growth, strong portable generator sales, and sharply higher in-home consultations. At the same time, residential energy storage sales declined. Management stated that “higher interest rates and a more challenging policy environment” continued to weigh on solar and storage demand and said investment in the category was being reduced.

The important read-through is the divergence between demand for resilience and customers’ willingness or ability to purchase solar-plus-storage systems. More outages and concern about reliability do not automatically overcome financing costs, installation complexity, or unfavorable policy economics. Those barriers can suppress equipment sell-through even while demand for other backup products improves.

For Enphase, the transmission is through residential installer activity and demand for microinverters and batteries. For SolarEdge, it is through inverter and storage demand, although its different geographic mix makes a US-heavy signal less directly transferable. Weaker sell-through can prolong channel inventory adjustment, constrain factory utilization, and increase promotional pressure. Cost reductions may protect profitability without establishing an end-market recovery.

The decline in Generac’s storage sales is not a clean industry demand measure because completion of the Puerto Rico Department of Energy program created a company-specific comparison. The higher-conviction sector signal is management’s separate commentary on financing and policy conditions, reinforced by its decision to reduce spending. The call also does not prove that generator buyers would otherwise have bought solar systems.

The near-term implication is caution toward treating improved outage activity as a catalyst for immediate residential solar equipment recovery. The longer-duration opportunity for storage remains intact

Soros-Backed PAC Helped Sweep ‘Woke Doctor’ Dems Into Congress | Gabrielle Fahmy & Shane Galvin, New York Post

A dark-money backed group funded by lefty kingmakers George Soros and his son Alex helped propel a record number of Democratic doctors and scientists into Congress, where they are expected to inject woke, identity-driven, leftist ideology into the nation’s health agenda next year.

Many of the 19 lawmakers voted in this week built careers on topics such as race, DEI, climate change and gun control as their No. 1 target.

The ideological army includes Dr. Annie Andrews (D-S.C.), a first-time politician whose campaign was considered a long shot before she won the Senate seat long held by the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, defeating his sister and successor, Sen. Darline Graham.

Andrews, 46, a pediatrician, has voiced her support for puberty blockers and cross-sex hormones for minors, proclaiming last year “gender affirming care isn’t child abuse” — and her 63 research papers includes a slew of political and identity-themed studies.

Even though her clinical specialty is asthma and that was the focus of her initial body of research, she took a decidedly woke turn around 2020, since then authoring nines studies on firearms alone, including a 2020 paper entitled “Pediatric Hospitalists at the Front Line of Gun Violence” that promoted responsible weapons storage

She also co-authored “Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Utilization of Tonsillectomy among Medicaid-Insured Children” in the Journal of Pediatrics in 2022, where she argued for developing “culturally appropriate interventions.”

In 2024, she penned an op-ed in JAMA titled “It is time to get political for children,” stating she was taking “a hard pivot into politics” for “the sick and injured kids I care for” because of gun safety, gender-affirming care and vaccines.

Richard Pan (D-Calif.), a pediatrician who won on his first bid for federal office, recruited Sacramento parents in 2015 to launch “Vaccinate California,” a campaign to ban personal-belief exemptions for school vaccine requirements. The measure became state law that year.

His research includes pro-DEI papers such as “Enhancing the Racial and Ethnic Diversity of the Pediatric Workforce” and “Nondiscrimination in Pediatric Health Care.”

Others include Jamie Ager (D-N.C.), who flipped a House seat in the Tar Heel State and has been touted as an “environmental scientist” even though his only science credential is an undergraduate degree in environmental studies and history from Warren Wilson College, a liberal arts school in North Carolina.

Terror-linked, Egyptian-born Dr. Adam Hamawy, a New Jersey plastic surgeon who volunteered in Gaza and won his House race, has faced scrutiny over his past ties to Islamic extremists.

Hamawy, 57, has been accused by the Investigative Project on Terrorism of lying under oath as a defense witness for “the Blind Sheikh” — the man behind the World Trade Center bombing in 1993 — whom he accompanied on a 1991 road trip to an Islamic conference in Detroit. He was never charged with perjury.

He also volunteered in Bosnia with a Chicago-based nonprofit whose offices were raided by the government in 2002 after it was determined to be a front for al-Qaeda — and has continued to dodge questions about his past associations with Islamist extremists.

Meanwhile as a doctor at home, he’s been described as a “creep” in reviews and sued for leaving a patient injured after a botched neck lift, according to a 2017 lawsuit.

Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.), who calls himself a physician even though he never completed his medical school residency and has never held a medical license, has his own share of race-obsessed medical research.

His papers include Columbia University research slammed as “eugenics” suggested Arab women should only breed with their own kind for optimal health outcomes.

The Post previously reported El-Sayed, 42 — whose medical degree was funded by a grant from the Soros family for new Americans — exploited identity politics in academia to fast-track and fund his journey to Congress.

“This is just the left trying to capitalize on their complete occupation and control of higher education and academia,” Theo Wold, former White House deputy assistant for domestic policy under Trump, told The Post.

“They want to use scientific credentials to hoodwink voters into trusting so-called scientific expertise that is just leftist ideology with a veneer of STEM terminology.”

The political action committee 3.14 Action says its mission is to “identify STEM leaders who would make strong candidates, recruit them to run for office and provide game-changing support.” It doubled its investment these midterms, spending $23 million on the candidates.

Its legislative priorities include abortion, climate change and gun violence.

The group has made no secret of its aversion to Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and his Make America Healthy Again movement — dubbing him their “number one villain.”

Democrats’ newly won House majority arms them with the power to subpoena witnesses for congressional investigations, which these newly elected candidates have made clear they intend to use against the MAHA leader.

Pan, 61, previously told reporters that grilling RFK Jr. under oath was one of his motivations for running for Congress. El-Sayed has already vowed to probe the Kennedy scion, while Andrews has pledged to impeach and remove him from office.

“RFK Jr. has been my professional archnemesis for decades, and there are thousands of pediatricians across the country who would say the same thing,” she blasted.

Far-left billionaires Alex and George Soros’ Open Society Action Fund gave $34.4 million to Our American Future Action in 2024, which contributed $9 million to House Majority Forward, which in turn donated $2.5 million to 3.14 Action, according to donation records.

The PAC grooms candidates from start to finish, not only recruiting woke scientists, but giving them training, staff support, polling, strategic guidance and money, according to 3.14’s website.

It produced more than 2,300 ads, which aired hundreds of thousands of times in October alone, with many promoting the candidates’ healthcare background, a Washington Post analysis found.

“If anyone is responsible for politicizing science, it’s Robert F. Kennedy Jr.,” 3.14 Action President Shaughnessy Naughton told The Post.

“As Health Secretary, he has continued his lifelong crusade against vaccines counter to decades of evidence, upended the FDA approvals process to green light pet projects and accelerate manufacturing of injectable peptides, kratom and candy flavored e-cigarettes.”

RFK Jr. did not return The Post’s request for comment.

@Uber built a giant on other people's cars. Its early robotaxis will sit on its own books.

With its third-quarter results on 4 November, Uber said it expects about 700 fully driverless vehicles on its network by the end of 2026 and more than 2,000 in 2027, both company targets. On the earnings call, executives said Uber will carry those early robotaxis on its own balance sheet.

Uber runs a global ride-hailing, delivery and freight platform that handled 4.1 billion trips in the quarter, per its results release.

The ownership choice is the real news. Executives said Uber will hold early vehicles because the resale value of a used robotaxi is still unproven, then hand them to outside financiers once that value is established.

The plan sits inside a multi-year autonomy commitment of more than $10 billion, which Uber first set out in August and ties to partner deliverables. Partners named on the call include Zoox and Motional in Las Vegas this quarter, and Nuro in California and Houston in early 2027.

The bigger picture: Uber is betting it can earn more from each robotaxi by keeping it busier. It says its US hybrid deployments show about a 30% utilisation premium over mature first-party deployments, and it aims for robotaxi margins to match human-driven trips over time.

Two thousand vehicles is still a pilot-sized fleet for a platform doing 4.1 billion trips a quarter. Uber has yet to size the profit impact of putting those vehicles on its own books.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE 
November 9, 2026

Conservative Action Network Launches Free Technology Tools to Expand Civic Participation and Reduce Barriers for Local Candidates

[Loudoun County, VA] — Conservative Action Network (CAN), a newly formed social welfare organization, today announced its launch to promote the common good by expanding civic engagement and reducing structural barriers that limit who can effectively participate in local and state elections. The organization will provide free software tools—where state law permits—that support direct voter contact and data-informed outreach, helping more community members run competitive races without the heavy intermediary costs that currently discourage participation.

CAN’s primary purpose is the promotion of social welfare through broader civic involvement. Any political activity is secondary and conducted in full compliance with federal and state law.

At a Glance

- Social welfare organization focused on expanded civic participation
- Free software tools for voter contact and data outreach (where state law allows)
- Goal: lower barriers so more community members can run and voters have more choices
- Seeking $5,000 in recurring monthly support to sustain the platform
- Website: https://t.co/mTWv0C9SRk

Why the 2026 Midterms Underscore the Need for Better Civic Infrastructure

The 2026 midterm elections follow repeated cycles in which high costs and limited tools have reduced competitive races and narrowed voter choice. In Virginia’s 2025 elections, Democrats swept every statewide office. Abigail Spanberger defeated Winsome Earle-Sears for Governor by roughly 57 percent to 42 percent. Ghazala Hashmi defeated John Reid for Lieutenant Governor by about 55 percent to 44 percent. Jay Jones defeated Jason Miyares for Attorney General by approximately 52 percent to 46 percent. Republicans failed to break 50 percent in any of those contests and underperformed both Donald Trump’s 2024 total and Glenn Youngkin’s 2021 total.

The same structural issues—uncontested seats, consultant-driven costs that consume half or more of contributions, and limited modern tools—have continued into the 2026 cycle. When local candidates face $10,000–$50,000 in service fees and statewide candidates face $50,000–$100,000 before they can effectively reach voters, fewer people run. When seats go uncontested, as 15 House of Delegates seats did in 2025 and 20 did in 2023, hundreds of thousands of voters lose the opportunity to choose. Midterms amplify these gaps because they depend heavily on local and state races where resources are thinner.

Aggressive modern technology can help reverse that pattern by lowering the cost of direct voter contact and data-informed outreach. Expanding the number of people who can participate as candidates increases competition, improves accountability, and gives voters more meaningful choices—core elements of stronger civic life.

A Twenty-Year Structural Imbalance Documented in The Blueprint

This effort is informed by the long-term structural reality documented in The Blueprint: How the Democrats Won Colorado (and Why Republicans Everywhere Should Care) by Adam Schrager and Rob Witwer. For roughly the last 20 years, progressive donors and organizations built coordinated infrastructure—beginning with the Colorado Democracy Alliance around 2004—that operates outside traditional party structures through nonprofits, data-driven targeting, and year-round operations. That model has been adapted across states, counties, and localities.

No comparable permanent civic infrastructure was built on the other side. The results in Virginia in 2025 and patterns visible in the 2026 midterms are consistent with one side operating sustained networks while the other continues to rely on high-cost consultants, incomplete recruitment, and tools that do not scale. Addressing that imbalance through practical technology that lowers barriers is one step toward restoring broader participation and meaningful voter choice. Time remains limited if communities want more competitive local races in the years ahead.

Ignored Approaches and Local Contrast

Four years ago, Scott Pio shared detailed approaches with then-Virginia GOP Chair on strengthening results in Virginia and expanding the House of Delegates majority. Last year he discussed comparable data and strategies with then Virginia GOP Chair focused on statewide competitiveness. Neither set of recommendations was adopted, and efforts were made to remove Pio as Loudoun County Republican Committee chair despite local gains. Also last year, Pio sat down with Senator Bryce Reeves and walked through data and voting mechanisms in Virginia along with what it would take to compete effectively for U.S. Senate. Within two weeks Reeves withdrew from the race.

Under Pio’s local leadership, the Loudoun County Republican Committee substantially increased membership and raised $1,200,000 —compared with roughly $20,000 annually before—while improving the county’s Republican position by 9 points. Those results showed that practical tools and consistent outreach can expand participation even in competitive areas. Broader application of data-driven and technology-supported approaches was largely not pursued at the state level.

“I am frustrated—deeply frustrated—with a system that lets consultants get rich while candidates and communities get shortchanged,” said founder Scott Pio. “We are done waiting for the same structures to fix themselves. Aggressive technology that puts tools directly in the hands of local candidates is how we expand real civic participation and give voters more choices.”

What Candidates Receive

CAN offers free software that supports direct voter contact, data-informed outreach, and efficient campaign operations to approved applicants in states that permit such assistance. In jurisdictions that restrict free software or in-kind support to candidates, the organization fully complies with applicable law and provides only legally permitted support. The tools are designed to reduce intermediary costs so candidates can focus resources on reaching voters. Application details and state-by-state compliance information are available on the organization’s website.

Call to Action

CAN is seeking $5,000 in recurring monthly support from individuals who share its commitment to expanded civic participation and more competitive local races. These funds will sustain the technology platform and related engagement efforts. These funds will FIRE many of the consultants we have grown to hate always getting paid while their candidates continue to lose.

Candidates and community groups preparing for the 2027 cycle and beyond can learn about the application process and available tools at https://t.co/29BtBh2m2v. Media inquiries and requests for founder availability or additional materials should be directed to the contact below.
For more information on the organization’s social welfare mission, priorities, or to contribute, visit https://t.co/29BtBh2m2v.

About Conservative Action Network

Conservative Action Network is a social welfare organization whose primary purpose is the promotion of the common good and general welfare of communities through expanded civic engagement, public education on constitutional republic participation, and aggressive modern technology that reduces barriers for candidates focused on local and state issues. It provides free software and support resources where permitted by law, with the aim of increasing the number of people who can effectively participate in the electoral process. Donations are not tax-deductible. More information is available at https://t.co/6gtzOUFLba.

Scott Pio 
Founder, Conservative Action Network

text:
Last week was an absolute bloodbath for the GOP. It was modeled off 2006 when George W. Bush entered a war with Iraq and it affected his midterms, but worse for Trump.

What's really sad is we sent some of our strongest candidates from the US House to run for higher office, not realizing their loss in the general election was inevitable from the beginning.

With that being said, last week should not be mistaken for some of the candidates' performance towards the general election. While there are incumbents I believe should not run again, there are some candidates, incumbent and non-incumbent, who could've won last week had the environment not been extremely unfavorable towards Republicans.

Part of this was due to the Senate GOP Leadership failing to pass the mandate given to them over the last 2 years, but it was mostly due to Trump breaking his promise that he would not start any new wars, making gas prices and housing prices go up when entering the Iran war, counteracting against the One Big Beautiful Bill passed. Because of this, it dragged down a ton of winnable races that should've been Safe R, and some Senate seats we won't be able to win back until 2032.

Should we have a chance to win again in 2028 and 2030, the best place to start is to nominate younger and charismatic candidates who can resonate with younger voters and bring young men back towards the GOP like Charlie Kirk did. Conservative propositions in some blue states like Colorado and Washington won last week, meaning the conservative ideologies aren't the losing issue, but the candidates who are weak on enforcing those ideologies did lose.

I absolutely like JD Vance and initially would've been thrilled to see him run for President, especially considering his debate performances for US Senate in 2022 and VP in 2024, but it seems unlikely he'll have a good chance to win due to some baggage Trump placed on him. Marco Rubio has been a great US Secretary to Trump with his foreign relations, but he's not someone I can see in the Oval Office in the future.

Ron DeSantis has been regaining his charisma and resonating the frustration that the grassroots movement experienced last week towards the RINOs that made this happen, even with me as someone who opposed his Presidential run in 2023 and 2024. That's why I'm currently leaning towards Ron DeSantis for President in 2028. If it wasn't for him, Florida wouldn't have survived the blue tsunami as other reliable Republican states did, and the only worst case scenario is that the blue seats meant to flip red after redistricting didn't flip. If Cory Mills was still the GOP candidate for FL-07, that seat would've flipped blue last week. God bless Ryan Elijah for stepping up to outprimary him and holding onto that seat for us.

Outprimary incumbents doesn't equal to instant loss as sometimes it's even necessary to win and shape the GOP's future. With all that said, we have the next 2 years to fight hard against the let's radical agenda in state level and federal level as Washington, DC enters the Lame Duck era. Texas has a huge fight ahead of them the next 2-4 years as they enter total Democrat control, and we need to fight like hell to preserve the border in that state or else we lose America for good.

If we can survive 8 years of Obama and 4 years of Biden, we will make it through the next 6 years. Like Charlie Kirk would want us to do if Kamala won in 2024, let's pick ourselves up and fight harder like never before!

TEXAS DEMOCRATS FILE TWIN HOUSE BILLS TO LEGALIZE RECREATIONAL MARIJUANA FOR ADULTS 21 & OLDER, ALLOWING UP TO 2 OUNCES POSSESSION, 12-PLANT HOME CULTIVATION & FULLY LICENSED RETAIL SALES

On The First Day Of Prefiling For The 90th Texas Legislature, Democratic State Representatives John Bucy III Of Austin & Joe Moody Of El Paso Introduced House Bills 362 & 369, Near-Identical Measures Titled The Texas Regulation Of Cannabis Act. A Companion Senate Bill 237 From Senator Carol Alvarado Of Houston Followed Shortly Afterward. The House Versions Would Authorize Adults 21 & Older To Use, Possess & Transport Not More Than 2 Ounces Of Cannabis, With No More Than 15 Grams Of That Amount In The Form Of Cannabis Concentrate, While Also Permitting Unpaid Transfers Of The Same Quantities Provided The Transfers Are Not Advertised Or Promoted To The Public.

Under The Official Bill Language, Adults Could Cultivate For Personal Use Not More Than 12 Cannabis Plants On The Premises Of A Private Residence, Provided Cultivation Occurs In An Enclosed Area Equipped With Locks Or Other Security Devices That Restrict Access & Is Not Visible From A Public Place Without The Use Of Aircraft Or Optical Aids. Harvested Cannabis From Those Plants Could Be Retained Along With Up To 10 Ounces Obtained Elsewhere, With Any Amount Exceeding 2 Ounces Stored Under Lock. The Measures Would Establish A Licensed Commercial System Covering Cannabis Growers, Establishments (Retail), Secure Transporters & Testing Facilities, Administered By The Texas Department Of Licensing & Regulation.

A 15% Tax Would Apply To Sales From Growers To Establishments & A 20% Tax To Retail Sales To Consumers, In Addition To Existing Sales Taxes. Proceeds Would Be Directed 50% To The Permanent School Fund, 25% To The Fund For Veterans’ Assistance, 15% To Chemical Dependency Prevention, Treatment & Rehabilitation, & 10% To Local Governments. Cities & Counties Could Regulate Hours, Locations & The Number Of Businesses But Could Not Prohibit Or Unreasonably Restrict Authorized Operations. If Enacted, The Act Would Take Effect September 1, 2027, With Implementing Rules Due By July 1, 2028 & Commercial Licensing Required To Begin By November 1, 2028.

The Filings Arrive One Week After Democrats Flipped Control Of The Texas House, Won The Governorship & Captured The Lieutenant Governor’s Office For The First Time In Decades, Ending Longtime Lieutenant Governor Dan Patrick’s Tenure. Republicans Retained A Senate Majority, Creating A Divided Legislature When The Session Convenes January 12, 2027. Prior Adult-Use Efforts Have Stalled In Austin Despite Growing Public Support & A Large Existing Market For Hemp-Derived Products, Meaning Passage Remains Uncertain Even With Democratic House Control & A Supportive Governor-Elect.

HOUSTON WE HAVE A BIG FCKNG PROBLEM AGAIN 

THE GREATEST CRIME IN HISTORY: AGAIN, AND AGAIN, AND AGAIN

Democracy presents its new season

HOLY SHIT!
THEY STOLE THE ELECTION AGAIN!
THIS HAS TO STOP!

That’s how the story begins: nuclear alarms, patriotic outrage, and the evidence arriving after the commercial.

According to this version, Republican votes stayed frozen since 2016. Not one stepped out for cigarettes!

The Democrats, the narrator claims, MATERIALIZED TWENTY MILLION VOTES. Entire countries with flags, anthems, and soccer teams popping out of a ballot box!
Right in front of artificial and military intelligence. All that intelligence, and nobody can find the remote!

I. DEMOCRACY WITH LARGE FRIES

Small-batch scandals won’t cut it anymore

I love this country. Nobody mass-produces scandal like America.
In Europe: “The minister accepted a free vacation.”
How adorable! Homegrown corruption from small local producers!

Here, we demand the SUPERSIZED, EXTRA-BULLSHIT COMBO WITH FREE REFILLS: Congress, spies, lawyers, retired generals, 47 anonymous sources, three documentaries, six podcasts, and some asshole screaming “BREAKING NEWS!” about something from four years ago.
The news has arthritis, but it’s still urgent!

I went to buy toothpaste, and some guy explained the Constitution like fantasy football:
“Article Two is my quarterback.”
I wanted cavity protection. I ended up fleeing a constitutional scholar with coupons.

II. THE NINE WIZARDS IN ROBES

Looking for democracy’s receipt

In this script, the Supreme Court reads the fine print:

“HOLY SHIT! THEY STOLE THE ELECTION!”

That’s the promised twist. The narrator’s already selling tickets!

STOLEN LIKE A HUBCAP IN NEW JERSEY!

Who are the script’s suspects? Not Vladimir eating Doritos in the basement.
Countries! Officials! Military brass! Flags! Desks with landing strips!
All cleared to know things they’ll forget before Congress.

And their patriotic lapel pins:

“RELAX: THIS LIE COMES PRE-SANITIZED.”

Put on that flag, and lying becomes a “collection discrepancy.” Bullshit just got security clearance!

III. ENTER THE HUMAN ALARM

January 6 and the season finale

According to the story, they pull off the biggest political trick since Caesar discovered the Senate’s knife collection.
Not one was for cutting cake!

Then they point at the guy yelling “THEFT!”
“YOU DID IT!”
Justice with frequent-flyer miles.
You report a robbery, and the cop says:
“Excellent testimony. Try on these prison stripes.”
“My rights?”
“In the laundry, with the evidence.”

IV. TREASON WITH A CONCIERGE

Economy class is for peasants

The accusation escalates to TREASON!
PENTHOUSE! CHAMPAGNE! CAVIAR!

Everyone gets a lawyer, a memoir, security clearance, and a TV contract.

In Washington, failure has a talent agent.
IT GETS YOU A PODCAST!
“You destroyed an institution?”
“Yes. Subscribe for my side.”

I committed treason eleven times: I’ve owed a library book since 1973. The librarian’s requested international backup!

V. THE GRAND FINALE

An outsourced presidency

The conspiracy’s ending? That theft, lies, investigations, leaks, and constitutional gymnastics were designed to let a FOREIGNER effectively govern.

Two hundred fifty years selling democracy, freedom, apple pie, eagles, and government of the people, only to end with:
“Fuck it. Let’s outsource the presidency!”

God bless America. And keep your receipt!

text:
Scam is a strong word. After last week’s midterms, Texas governor elect Gina Hinojosa is promising to tear down the state’s new school voucher program, one of Gov. Greg Abbott’s biggest wins.

According to a joint report Saturday from The Texas Tribune and ProPublica, Texas this year launched the program and about 110,000 of the state’s more than 5 million schoolchildren now use taxpayer dollars for a private education. The Dallas Express, citing the state’s October 1 report, put the number of funded accounts at 116,574, and said about 62 percent of those families live at or below 200 percent of the federal poverty level. Published awards are $10,474 a year for a participating private school student. The current budget sets aside $1 billion through August 31, 2027.

“We will work tirelessly to repair the damage of the Texas voucher scam,” Hinojosa said in her victory speech, the Tribune and ProPublica reported. She also pledged to fire Texas Education Agency Commissioner Mike Morath and end the state’s public school takeovers. Repealing the program would take a vote of the Legislature. Democrats won the Texas House for the first time in 24 years, the Tribune reported, but Republicans kept the Senate and can block a repeal. The Dallas Express reported that Hinojosa cannot wipe out this year’s budget, though she could veto later funding, and that this year’s payments are still scheduled, including a February 1 installment.

Comptroller elect Sarah Eckhardt told the Tribune she will audit how the money is spent and report back to lawmakers, but that any big overhaul has to come from the Legislature. Rep. Diego Bernal, the Democratic vice chair of the House education committee, told the Tribune he expects the program to be heavily rewritten or gone by the time lawmakers finish. Houston Republican Sen. Paul Bettencourt, who helped pass the law, said the Senate should review this first year’s results before anyone decides the program’s future. The Tribune reported that at least 13 Republicans Abbott backed in his voucher fight lost or were trailing after Tuesday.

A scam is fraud, not a program the Legislature passed and more than 100,000 families already use. If lawmakers want to change it, they should vote in the open and look at the results first. Don’t pull the rug out from under those kids.

Sources: The Texas Tribune and ProPublica; The Dallas Express

text:
I Asked My Wife for Sex Every Morning Before Work. By Thursday, She Was Avoiding Me.

I thought I had discovered the secret to a perfect marriage.

Whenever my wife and I made love before she left for work, I felt happier, more relaxed, and unusually confident throughout the day. Even the worst meetings seemed easier to handle.

So I decided to make it a daily routine.

I didn't realise that what started as a playful request would soon make my wife dread hearing the alarm.

One night, while we were lying in bed after dinner, I turned toward her.

Me: “I've noticed something.”

Wife: “What now?”

Me: “Whenever we have sex in the morning, my whole day feels lighter. I get to work in a better mood, I'm less stressed, and even traffic doesn't annoy me as much.”

She laughed.

Wife: “So?”

Me: “So I want us to do it every morning.”

She lifted her head from the pillow.

Wife: “Every morning?”

Me: “Every single morning.”

Wife: “You're joking.”

I kissed her shoulder.

Me: “I'm serious. Why are you looking at me like I've just asked you to run a marathon?”

She shook her head, smiling.

Wife: “Baby, do you understand what you're asking? I have to wake up early, shower, get dressed, prepare breakfast, and deal with traffic. You want to add another activity to my morning routine?”

Me: “You're my wife. Who else am I supposed to ask?”

She laughed again.

Wife: “I thought marriage was supposed to give me some peace.”

Me: “This is peace. You'll leave the house happier, and I'll have a good day.”

She gave me a suspicious look.

Wife: “And what happens when I'm tired?”

I grinned.

Me: “Then I'll have to be very convincing.”

She hit my arm with a pillow.

Wife: “You better learn to take no for an answer.”

We eventually negotiated like two people settling a workplace agreement. I wanted five mornings a week. She offered two. After plenty of teasing, we settled on four, with weekends off so she could “recover.”

At the time, I thought I'd struck an excellent deal.

Monday morning was wonderful. We woke up a little earlier, shared some intimacy, showered, and had breakfast together. She left for work smiling, and I spent the entire morning feeling like the luckiest husband alive.
Tuesday was just as good.

By Wednesday, however, I began noticing small changes.

She started setting her alarm earlier. Sometimes she'd remain under the shower longer than usual. One morning, she said her back was hurting. Another morning, she simply rolled over and pulled the blanket over her head.

I tried to joke about our agreement.

Me: “Madam, I believe we have a commitment.”

She opened one eye.

Wife: “And I believe I need another hour of sleep.”

I laughed, but I could tell she wasn't enjoying the routine as much as I was.

NVIDIA -6%:

US futures fell as Nvidia’s leadership crisis hit the AI trade: Nasdaq 100 contracts lost 1% and S&P 500 futures fell 0.5%. MSCI Asia Pacific down 0.8%, the Hang Seng down 1.3% and Shanghai down 0.8%, while Euro Stoxx 50 futures rose 0.2%. (BBG)

Alibaba fell as much as 7.1% in Hong Kong as the Nvidia scandal renewed concerns about Chinese firms’ access to advanced chips. https://t.co/giNUCibwEV and MiniMax each fell at least 7%. (BBG)

Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom each gained more than 3% after hours on expectations they could win business from Nvidia’s turmoil. Alphabet rose 0.3% as investors considered alternatives to Nvidia’s AI accelerators. (BBG)

Nvidia directors were preparing to remove Jensen Huang, WSJ reported, following reports of affairs with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset and healthcare VP Kimberly Powell. No completed removal decision has yet been confirmed. (WSJ, FT)

Nvidia engaged an outside firm to find successors, Bloomberg reported. Some directors favour CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO and have discussed adding a COO, while Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji is being considered for the permanent role, Semafor reported. (BBG, Semafor)

US Commerce department is finalising Chinese remote-access curbs for Blackwell and newer chips, possibly this month, The Information reported. Proposed licensing would extend to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Brazil, Norway and South Africa. (The Information)

US-operated data centres in those markets would avoid chip-import licensing if they bar access by arms-embargoed countries and report customers and capacity. Commerce also plans formal repeal of the AI Diffusion Rule. (The Information)

Chinese AI companies are approaching overseas data-centre operators to reserve Nvidia computing capacity, fearing tighter US remote-access controls, Reuters reports. Grey-market buyers inside China are also stockpiling restricted processors amid concerns about tougher enforcement. (RTRS)

The suspected Chinese spy at the center of the scandal (Alice Huang) has returned to Beijing, according to Bloomberg sources. It wasn’t immediately clear when or why she traveled to the capital, nor what she may be engaged in.  (BBG)

Elon Musk said it would be an “honor” to hire Jensen Huang if he is removed from Nvidia. (Musk)

'Nvidia’s Disappearing Singapore Sales Deepen Mystery Around Megaspeed' WSJ article notes Nvidia switched its geographic revenue reporting from billing addresses to customer headquarters after blocking Megaspeed in June 2025. Singapore, previously 22% of sales, disappeared as a separate category. (WSJ)

Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons asked Lutnick, Rubio and White House chief of staff Stephen Miller to preserve records covering Nvidia’s China exports and Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. They requested confirmation by Tuesday that staff had been instructed to retain the material. (WSJ)

Some Trump administration officials had privately warned that Huang’s lobbying for China chip sales undermined national security, WSJ reported. Officials opposing his approach were sidelined or left, while David Sacks and Howard Lutnick helped sustain Huang’s influence with Trump, people familiar said. (WSJ)

Alibaba was an anchor customer behind Megaspeed’s successful push for priority access as an Nvidia cloud partner in November 2023, people familiar told WSJ. Megaspeed supplied Alibaba with computing power from Nvidia servers housed in Malaysia. (WSJ)

Nvidia customer Megaspeed shipped some restricted chips into China, including to Shanghai cloud provider Century Litong, WSJ reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Megaspeed says it complies with applicable export controls. (WSJ)

'Megaspeed's links to rural Australian store raise fresh questions in Nvidia scandal' Reuters article notes Megaspeed registered overseas affiliates using a director whose listed address is a rural Victorian newsagency. Australian and Delaware filings identify Kai Kang as the sole officer; Reuters could not establish whether Australian authorities are investigating the company. (RTRS)

Beijing said Washington should stop using the Huang allegations as a pretext for technology restrictions. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said China remains in contact with US counterparts ahead of next week’s leaders’ meeting. (BBG)
